# /ccc-plan — plan file template

The planner agent writes this shape to `PLAN_PATH`. The trace comment is the first line. Both evals sections are required; the done-evals use the `— check:` form so `sprint-contract.mjs from-plan` can read them.

````markdown
<!-- generated by /ccc-plan · <ISO 8601 timestamp> -->
# <Feature title>

**Date:** <YYYY-MM-DD>
**Path:** <new | bug | refactor | linear>
**Branch:** <current branch or "none">
**Linear:** <issue key or "none">

## Problem statement

<2-3 sentences, plain English.>

## Evals — what does done look like?

These bullets become the sprint contract (`tasks/sprint-contract.md`) after approval; the verifier agent checks each one with fresh context before the work is called done. One observable criterion per bullet, at most ten.

- [ ] <observable criterion> — check: `<command that exits 0 only when it holds>`
- [ ] <observable criterion> — check: `<command>`
- [ ] <behavior with no single command> — check: manual — <what to observe>

## Evals — what does broken look like?

- <failure mode 1>
- <failure mode 2>

## Plan

### Phase 1 — <name>
- [ ] <step> (est. <time>)
- [ ] <step> (est. <time>)

### Phase 2 — <name>
- [ ] <step>

### Phase 3 — <name>
- [ ] <step>

## Execution

Delegate substantive steps to agents or workflows per `rules/workflow-first.md`. A checker independent of the step's worker verifies each phase.

## Recommended agents

- **<agent>** — <why>

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| <risk> | H/M/L | <one line> |

## Next command

```
/ccc-build contract   # or /ccc-plan-exec for repeated per-item work, /ccc-review, /ccc-ship
```
````
